# Manual CIP assignment from approximate 2D drawing coordinates (y up = -image_y)
import numpy as np
def chirality(center, subs, priorities):
    # subs: dict name-> (x,y,z) with z: +1 wedge(front), -1 dash(back), 0 plane
    c = np.array(subs[center]); 
    vecs = {k: np.array(subs[k]) - c for k in subs if k!=center}
    # implicit H: opposite of sum, on side opposite to any dash/wedge explicit
    s = sum(vecs.values())
    h = -s
    # if an explicit sub has z!=0, H gets opposite z sign component
    zs = [vecs[k][2] for k in vecs if abs(vecs[k][2])>0]
    hz = -zs[0] if zs else 0
    h = np.array([h[0], h[1], hz if hz!=0 else 0.0])
    if np.linalg.norm(h)<1e-6: h=np.array([0,0,1.0])
    a,b,d = [vecs[p] for p in priorities]
    n = np.cross(b-a, d-b)
    # view from opposite of h: sign of n . (-h)
    val = np.dot(n, -h)
    return "R" if val<0 else "S", val
